top_strength: When the customer apologized for her English making the call harder to follow, Alexander immediately reassured her — "you're actually being very helpful right now... no worries right there, you're doing just fine" — which kept her comfortable enough to keep giving details through a genuinely difficult intake (~1,900 sqft home, right at the one-truck/two-truck cutoff).
coaching_note: Alexander never opened with an agenda statement (no "I'll gather some details, then walk you through pricing, sound good?") and only used the customer's name twice, both near the very end ("that Ruby, I'm gonna...", "thank you, Ruby") — leading with the agenda and using her name earlier would have given this language-barrier-heavy call more structure and warmth from the start.
phone_presence_notes: Stayed calm and reassuring through repeated miscommunication (square footage, fragile items, the garage), explicitly telling the customer she was doing fine rather than showing frustration, though the call stayed mostly task-focused with no humor or rapport beyond the task.
audio_review_reason: Customer's transcribed speech shows a heavy language barrier with frequent garbled/unclear passages (e.g., sqft given as "11889"), which limits how reliably tone can be judged from text alone — worth an audio check to confirm the rep's patience read the same way in voice as it does on the page.
